Server preferences read back charts_workspace_layout.widgets[uctd-chart].opts = {tf:'W', settings:{chartType:'bars'}} and charts_workspace_groups = {"A":"AAPL","B":null,"C":null,"D":null}.
result: ⭐⭐ ONE SHARED SERVER-BACKED WORKSPACE ALREADY EXISTS — a phone edit lands on the desktop board
notes: ⛔⛔ THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT P9 FACT AND IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS RECOMMENDATION. The instinct is 'UCT needs a saved-workspace model like TradingView's'. It HAS one, it is server-backed, and mobile is already a first-class writer to it. What it lacks is NAMING, SNAPSHOTTING and SCOPING — see UCT-P9-0003 and UCT-P9-0007. Verified on both surfaces AND in the persisted record, so this is not an inference from source.

action: Read charts_workspace_layout and charts_workspace_groups after a phone-side symbol change
response: Every widget in charts_workspace_layout carries hasSym:false — the widgets record type, id, colour group and per-widget opts (tf, chart settings), never a ticker. The ticker lives once per COLOUR GROUP in charts_workspace_groups: {"A":"AAPL","B":null,"C":null,"D":null}.
result: ⭐ THE SYMBOL IS A VARIABLE INSIDE THE LAYOUT, EXACTLY AS P9 PREDICTED — and it is already server-backed
notes: ⭐ P9 was stated as 'the layout is the durable object; the symbol is a variable inside it'. UCT's data model ALREADY expresses that, and expresses it more cleanly than TradingView's: TV binds a symbol per chart pane and links panes by colour AFTER the fact; UCT stores exactly four ticker slots and every widget dereferences one. The four-slot ceiling is the cost — see the register entry on colour groups.

action: Read the tracings_doc server preference and trace the sync layer and its mount point
response: tracings_doc holds {updatedAt, doc} where doc = {v, tracings[], activeId, visibleIds, byTracing}. On this account it reads byTracing.default.SPY = 2 drawings. app/src/components/chart/useTracingsSync.js bridges the localStorage drawings store to that preference: hydrate-newer-wins on first load, debounced 1500ms push on change, flush on unmount. exportTracings() sets byTracing[activeId] = loadAll(), so the ACTIVE sheet's per-symbol drawings are inside the synced blob, not just the archived sheets. The hook is called at ChartsWorkspace.jsx:662 — ABOVE the isMobile branch at :2051 — so it runs on the phone shell too.
result: ⛔ CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER NOTE — DRAWINGS ARE SERVER-SYNCED, ON BOTH SURFACES
notes: ⛔⛔ SUPERSEDES the earlier working note that 'uct-chart-drawings is localStorage-only, so drawings are device-local'. That was true of the KEY and false of the SYSTEM: the localStorage map holds the ACTIVE sheet, and the active sheet is exported into the synced document. This is the third time in this study that reading one storage location produced a false negative about a capability. ⭐ Net effect on the comparison: UCT is at PARITY with TradingView on cross-device drawing persistence, not behind it. Do not carry a 'drawings do not follow the user' claim anywhere.

target: A defect in the drawing-sync highwatermark
action: Compare this browser's uct-tracings-sync-hw against the server's tracings_doc.updatedAt, and read the push path that writes the highwatermark
response: LIVE STATE: hw = 1788827970231, server updatedAt = 1788827970231, difference 0. The hydrate gate is `server.updatedAt > hw` (STRICT), so wouldAdoptServer is FALSE. Local uct-chart-drawings reads '{}' — no drawings — while the server document holds SPY:2. SOURCE: flushPush() computes updatedAt, writes it to lastPushedRef, calls writeHW(updatedAt), and THEN calls setPref(...). The setPref result is neither awaited nor checked.
result: ⛔ A DEVICE CAN BE PERMANENTLY PINNED PAST A SERVER COPY IT NEVER TOOK — observed live
notes: ⚠️ STATE THIS PRECISELY, IT IS EASY TO OVERCLAIM. (a) The MECHANISM is source-verified: the highwatermark is advanced before an unawaited write, and the adopt gate is strict '>', so a device is pinned at exactly the version it believes it pushed. (b) The DIVERGENCE is live-verified on this browser: server holds two drawings, the device holds none, and the device will never adopt them. (c) The TRIGGERING PATH IN A REAL USER'S HANDS IS INFERRED — my local copy was most likely emptied by an abruptly destroyed probe iframe, which is not a member path. Plausible real equivalents (a failed or aborted push, a quota-failed write, cleared site data on one device) are UNTESTED. ⛔ Do not report this as a known member-facing outage. Report it as a defect in the durable-state layer with a live reproduction on a research device, and fix the ordering (write the highwatermark only after a confirmed write) regardless of how often it fires.

target: Pan/zoom view state — where it lives
action: Enumerate localStorage on the charts surface and trace the key back to source
response: localStorage holds uct.charts.viewLock.uctd-chart (85 bytes). origin/master:app/src/components/StockChart.jsx:1780 documents viewLockKey as 'localStorage key. When set (Charts workspace), the user's pan/zoom/price-scale view is PERSISTED here so it survives a page refresh — restored on load, cleared by Reset view'; ChartPane.jsx:864 keys it `uct.charts.viewLock.${chartId}`.
result: ⚠️ SPLIT DURABILITY — the widget id is SERVER-backed, the view of that widget is DEVICE-local
notes: ⭐ THIS IS THE CLEANEST EXAMPLE OF THE P9 PROBLEM SHAPE. One conceptual object — 'my chart' — is stored in two places with two lifetimes and two scopes: arrangement + timeframe + settings + symbol on the server, pan/zoom on the device. Restore a workspace on a second device and you get the board back framed on a different range. Neither half is wrong on its own; the SPLIT is what has no owner. ⭐ It is also defensible as the DEFAULT (a phone and a 32-inch monitor should not share a pixel range) — which is exactly why the fix is a per-device SCOPE inside one record, not a move of the key.

target: _COARSE_POINTER is decided once, at module load
action: Read the only real coarse-pointer gate in the drawing overlay
response: ChartDrawingOverlay.jsx:83-90 defines `const _COARSE_POINTER = typeof window !== 'undefined' && !!window.matchMedia?.('(pointer: coarse)')?.matches` at MODULE scope, and derives HIT_THRESHOLD (15 vs 8), HANDLE_R (7 vs 4), auto-select-after-placement (:2158), the coach chip (:2642), DrawingQuickBar (:2686) and sheet={_COARSE_POINTER} (:2735) from it.
result: ⚠️ A ONE-SHOT READ OF A LIVE MEDIA QUERY — every touch affordance in the drawing layer hangs off it
conf: NATIVE_VERIFIED (the code shape) + INFERRED_NOT_VERIFIED (the device consequence)
notes: ⚠️ THE CONSEQUENCE IS INFERRED AND MUST BE LABELLED SO — I did not test an iPad with a Magic Keyboard attached and detached. (pointer: coarse) is a LIVE query: on an iPad it flips when a trackpad keyboard is attached or removed, and matchMedia would report the change to a listener. A module constant cannot hear it, so until a full reload the drawing layer keeps the grab radii, the auto-select, the quick bar and the sheet-vs-popover choice of whatever pointer was present when the bundle evaluated. ⭐ This also explains, mechanically, why the whole fine-pointer lane produced false negatives: the constant is decided once per document, so a resized desktop frame can never become a touch surface no matter how narrow it gets. Cheap fix: a hook over the same query (useHasCoarsePointer already exists in useBreakpoint.js) instead of a constant.

target: What a reload keeps and what it drops
action: Reload the charts surface with drawings present and read both the drawing store and the undo/redo affordances
response: The DRAWINGS survive a reload; the HISTORY does not — after a reload both Undo and Redo render disabled, so the last action before the reload is unrecoverable. (Recorded in full at UCT-UNDO-0003, which also establishes that Redo fails to arm on the first undo after a load and works later in the same session.)
result: DRAWINGS PERSIST, HISTORY RESETS — the object is durable, the transaction log is not
notes: ⚠️ TIER NOTE: this was measured in the 390px FINE-POINTER frame, and the fine-pointer lane has produced three false negatives in this study. It is retained because the mechanism is storage-level, not input-level — the history lives in a module registry (drawingsStore's per-sym past/future arrays) that is not part of either persisted key, so no pointer type can change the answer. Cited as the reason it is not being re-run on hardware.
